question: Does spatially anchored read-in improve speed decoding beyond equally diverse arbitrary and depth-matched groups?
dataset: Stringer MP019, same repeatedly examined recording; exploratory only
architecture: 16 read-in queries: first8 restricted to8 groups except global control, last8 unrestricted; same16-query transformer, mean pooling, width32, head4, IDs and real xyz embedding in ALL arms
patches: Recursive coordinate threshold splits depth then x then y; threshold between distinct values closest to balanced cell counts; no physical distance assumptions
controls: random permutes spatial group labels across cells preserving exact group sizes; depth_random permutes labels within each imaging plane preserving exact group-by-plane counts; group assignment independent of labels and activity
causal_scope: Effect of spatial grouping conditional on true-coordinate token embeddings; not an ablation of all geometry
training: Same chronological splits, train-only activity/speed normalization, window8, width32, AdamW .001 weight_decay.01, batch32, cosine24 eta_min.0001, clip1, min12/patience7, select best validation boundedMSE including epoch0
initialization: Construct existing8-query Candidate then append8 queries using independent seeded generator; shared parameters equal existing baseline; exact initial state and batch order across4arms
budget: All48 planned before observing new outcomes; no seed, architecture, or epoch changes based on outcomes
analysis: Raw and bounded MSE, R2, per-repeat/pool wins; paired crossed pool/seed circular-time-block100 bootstrap2000 for conditional95% intervals; exploratory and not biological replication
success: Candidate evidence: spatial mean MSE lower than both random controls and global, with >=8/12 pair wins against each. Stronger within-recording evidence: all3 paired intervals above0 and >=5/6 positive pool means. No cross-animal claim. No multiple-testing corrected claims.
mechanism: Audit group attention supports, query diversity, gradients, joint neuron-permutation invariance, attention mask perturbations, and trained dependence on local read-in using ablation. Artificial data positive control for known regional interactions.
